introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (English Language 1, June 2025, Ordinary Level, code 0530). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. The paper has four sections: A listening comprehension (questions 1-10), B reading comprehension (questions 11-25), C grammar (questions 26-40) and D vocabulary (questions 41-50).
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Questions ouvertes (clé non établie avec certitude ou option fautive) : Q1 (D anywhere contre C in the bus and on social media), Q13 (A loved and saved people contre B smelled lost people / D discovered people), Q17 (B job the dog does contre D help the dog renders), Q24 (aucune option n'est exacte : ni chanteurs ni écrivains dans le texte ; C est la plus proche), Q29 (aucune option ne donne sisters-in-law), Q37 (A History/Mathematics en majuscules contre B history/mathematics en minuscules), Q46 (D laid contre C put).

Clés retenues mais moins sûres : Q2 (B, l'option imprimée est fautive : carefully and wisdom), Q3 (C personal opinion ; concurrente A understanding of someone), Q5 (C fake ; concurrentes B pretentious et D unhappy), Q7 (C treatment ; concurrente D adviser), Q10 (C marriage counsellor ; concurrente B parent), Q20 (A left out ; concurrente B disappointed), Q39 (C ; D he had been living est aussi acceptable).
Questions 6 et 9 : le sujet imprime deux versions (EITHER / OR). La version EITHER est la question notée ; la version OR est recopiée dans l'énoncé avec sa réponse dans le corrigé.

Q43 : l'option B est imprimée « pumpous » (faute pour pompous) et Q48 l'option C « antangonistic » (faute pour antagonistic) ; recopiées telles quelles. Q44 : les options B, C, D sont des fautes d'orthographe voulues.

Le texte de l'écoute (Section A) vient des pages d'instructions du professeur, recopié sans les barres obliques de pause et sans les consignes de conduite. Les titres Section One/Two/Three correspondent aux questions 1-4, 5-7 et 8-10 du livret.

Les numéros de ligne des passages de lecture sont repris entre crochets en fin de ligne imprimée ; le titre souligné The History and Magic of the Dog n'est pas souligné (Markdown). Les mots soulignés des questions 41 à 43 sont rendus en gras.
Les sections de grammaire (26-36) et de vocabulaire (41-50) sont recopiées avec leurs consignes ; Q26 à Q36 : l'en-tête de section est dans l'énoncé de la Q26.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Listening passage (read aloud once by the examiner in the real exam - read it once, then answer)**

**Choosing a life partner**

**Section One**

My dear young people, you will soon be faced with the problem of choosing your life partners. I will like to give you my humble and candid advice and useful tips on how to go about it. You can meet your partner anywhere. Some meet in the bus, while some meet on social media. What matters most is the person you choose to marry, not where you met. The choice you make affects your destiny positively or negatively, so think well, then choose carefully and wisely.

Marriage is a mystery and cannot be entered into just by depending on the feelings that we have. Love is not just feelings. Choosing a life partner is deeply personal, enormously complicated and different for everyone. It is almost impossible to understand from the outside, no matter how well you know someone. As such, other people's opinions and preferences about who you choose really have no place, except in extreme cases involving maltreatment or abuse.

**Section Two**

These are some guidelines in choosing a life partner. Never be in a rush. Also, a great sense of humour must be there, because nobody wants to spend many long years with a partner faking laughter. The partner must be able to extract fun out of unappealing situations like airport delays, long drives and errands, visit to the village, and over-bearing in-laws. Studies suggest that the amount of fun a couple has is a strong predictor of their future and how long their relationship will last. Again, respect for each other's ideas, brains and ways of thinking is very important for a happy and successful marriage.

A life partner doubles as a career and life therapy. If you do not respect the way your partner thinks, you are not going to tell him/her your thoughts on work and things that happen to you in secret each day, or on anything else interesting that pops into your head.

**Section Three**

In order to have a long lasting relationship with your partner, you should avoid perpetual discomfort or situations that cause unhappiness. There should be trust and security to enable you feel safe, cosy, natural and utterly yourself.

Secrets are poison to a relationship because they form an invisible wall inside the relationship, leaving both partners alone in their world. Also, secrets often lead to suspicion and mistrust. This is why having an affair when married is one of the most self-defeating and short-sighted things someone could ever do. So take time to think well before choosing a partner.

**Section A - Listening comprehension (5 marks).** Using only the material read to you from the Listening Comprehension passage, answer each of the following questions as directed. Choose the best answer from the alternatives (A, B, C and D) for each of the questions below.

**Section One**

1. According to the passage, people meet their partners \_\_\_\_\_\_.

*Options as printed:* A) in the bus   B) on social media   C) in the bus and on social media   D) anywhere
questions.corrige_markdown:
The speaker says "You can meet your partner anywhere. Some meet in the bus, while some meet on social media." Option D repeats the general statement, while option C repeats the two examples that follow it. Both are faithful to the passage, and A and B are only half of the examples. Because the Board's key could be either D or C, this question is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**Answer: anywhere (D) is the general statement; "in the bus and on social media" (C) is also supported by the passage.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section One

2. When choosing a partner, \_\_\_\_\_\_ is very important.
questions.corrige_markdown: The speaker ends the first part with "think well, then choose carefully and wisely". Option B is the only one that matches this advice (the printed "carefully and wisdom" is a faulty version of "care and wisdom"). Love and feelings are rejected ("Love is not just feelings"), and understanding and prayers are never recommended. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section One

3. The choice of a partner chiefly depends on your \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The speaker says that choosing a partner "is deeply personal" and that "other people's opinions and preferences ... really have no place", so the choice rests on one's own opinion. Parents' opinion is excluded, feelings alone are not enough ("cannot be entered into just by depending on the feelings"), and understanding someone from the outside is called "almost impossible". **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section One

4. In the expression "enormously complicated" read/signed to you from the passage, "complicated" is a/an \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Complicated" describes how personal the choice is ("enormously complicated"), and it is modified by the adverb "enormously". A word that describes a quality is an adjective. It is not the noun ("complication"), and it is used here as a describing word, not as a verb or an interjection. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

5. According to the passage, a marriage in which someone spends many years faking laughter is a/an \_\_\_\_\_\_ marriage.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says nobody wants "to spend many long years with a partner faking laughter". Someone who fakes laughter produces a fake (false) marriage atmosphere, and the question reuses the word "faking". "Fun-filled" is the opposite of the idea, "pretentious" means showing off, and "unhappy" is a consequence that the speaker never states. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

6. (EITHER) You heard the word "guidelines" read to you from the passage. Which word below has the same number of syllables as in the word "guidelines"?

*Alternative version printed in the paper (OR):* "Guidelines" according to the passage are \_\_\_\_\_\_. A) commands   B) directives   C) instructions   D) posters
questions.corrige_markdown:
"Guidelines" has two syllables: guide-lines. "Guileless" also has two (guile-less), while "glamorous" (glam-or-ous), "gurrilla" (gue-rril-la) and "goalscorer" (goal-scor-er) have three. **Answer: B.**

Answer to the alternative (OR) version: "These are some guidelines in choosing a life partner" introduces pieces of advice, so guidelines are instructions (C); commands and directives are too forceful and posters are not mentioned.
themes: O Level English - syllables and sounds

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

7. \_\_\_\_\_\_ has the same meaning as the word "therapy" read/signed to you from the passage.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Therapy" means the treatment of a problem, so its synonym is "treatment". A companion and an adviser are people, and a solution is the answer to a problem, not the remedy process. In the passage the partner is the person to whom one tells one's thoughts, which is a kind of emotional treatment. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms
O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Three

8. According to the passage \_\_\_\_\_\_ becomes poison to a relationship.
questions.corrige_markdown: The speaker says "Secrets are poison to a relationship because they form an invisible wall". Suspicion and mistrust are only the result of secrets. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Three

9. (EITHER) You heard the word "utterly" read to you from the passage. Which word below has the same sound as the one underlined in **u**tterly?

*Alternative version printed in the paper (OR):* Those who desire long lasting relationships must avoid \_\_\_\_\_\_. A) situations that cause unhappiness   B) being lonely   C) perpetual comfort   D) trust
questions.corrige_markdown:
The underlined "u" in "utterly" is the short vowel /ʌ/ (as in "cup"). The first "o" of "otherwise" (/ˈʌðəwaɪz/) has the same sound. "Utensil" begins with /juː/, and "audible" and "orphanage" begin with /ɔː/. **Answer: A.**

Answer to the alternative (OR) version: the speaker says to "avoid perpetual discomfort or situations that cause unhappiness", so the answer is A (C reverses the idea: it should be discomfort, not comfort).
themes: O Level English - syllables and sounds

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Three

10. The speaker in this passage is likely a \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The speaker addresses "my dear young people", offers "advice and useful tips", gives "guidelines" and refers to studies, which fits a marriage counsellor. A friend or a parent would speak to one person or to their own children, and a researcher would present findings, not advice. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section B - Reading comprehension (7½ marks).** Read the following passages and answer the questions which follow.

**Passage A** (questions 11 to 18; the numbers in square brackets are the line numbers printed in the paper, placed at the end of the printed line)

Dogs and cats are very well suited to be our pets. They can be highly intelligent and extremely loyal and devoted to their human masters. From the very beginning, dogs were used to help people search for food. Dogs aided in the hunt for deer and wild pigs. They also made **excellent** guards, protecting their masters from danger with their keen hearing, eyesight, and sense of smell. Cats have offered important protection against mice and rats. [5]

Some of the most fascinating stories about dogs and cats tell about their special devotion to their masters. A dog that is especially well known for its love for humans is the St. Bernard. It was discovered that the St. Bernard's remarkable sense of smell was also useful for discovering people who were lost in mountain snowstorms.

In the late 1800s, a famous St. Bernard named Barry, saved forty travellers who had lost their way in [10] Mount Blizzards. Unfortunately, he was killed while trying to save the forty-first lost traveller. The traveller, probably **dazed** by cold, thought Barry was a bear coming to attack him, and killed the dog in self-defence.

Other dogs, such as German Shepherds, can be trained to help humans who have lost their sight. In his book, The History and Magic of the Dog, Fernand Mery tells the story of a blind French girl who took her [15] little puppy on her errands through the streets of her town. Bit by bit, the puppy learned how to wait for the light at the corner to change before crossing the street. As it grew older, the dog would move to avoid fire hydrants and other objects in the girl's path. In this way, it began signaling the girl that she should walk around these obstacles too.

One of the most amazing things about dogs and cats is their ability to find their way home from miles [20] away. A dog named Piglet, **because of his tracking**, helped two people to get married. Piglet's master often took Piglet to visit his girlfriend. One day they argued and decided never to see each other again. Several days later, Piglet appeared at the girl's door. Of course, Piglet had to be returned to his master. The master and his girlfriend made up, and later, they got married. **Piglet smiled and rejoiced on the day of their marriage.** [25]

**Questions 11 to 18**

11. From the passage, dogs and cats have the following qualities, except \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says dogs helped people search for food, protected their masters and were specially devoted to them. No animal trains its master to marry: Piglet only helped two people marry by finding the way to the girl's door. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: being used to help people search for food
training their masters when they want to marry
being specially devoted to their masters

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 12. The word "excellent" (line 3) is a/an \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Excellent" describes the noun "guards" ("excellent guards"), so it is an adjective. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage A above) 13. The St. Bernard was a special dog which \_\_\_\_\_\_.

*Options as printed:* A) loved and saved people   B) smelled lost people   C) cared for humans   D) discovered people
questions.corrige_markdown:
The passage says the St. Bernard is "especially well known for its love for humans" and that its sense of smell was "useful for discovering people who were lost", and Barry saved forty travellers. Option A combines the love and the rescues, but B (smelled lost people), C (cared for humans) and D (discovered people) each paraphrase one sentence of the paragraph. Since the Board's key is not known, this question is left open for self-assessment.

**Answer: loved and saved people (A) is the most complete; B, C and D are each supported by one sentence.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 14. According to the passage, a dog that is trained to help visually impaired humans is a \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Other dogs, such as German Shepherds, can be trained to help humans who have lost their sight." The St. Bernard finds lost people, Piglet helped two people marry, and Charlie is not in the passage. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 15. In the passage, the common attribute for dogs and cats is that, they \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first sentence applies to both animals: "They can be highly intelligent and extremely loyal and devoted to their human masters." Only cats protect against mice and rats, and nothing is said about magic or mystery. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: can be protective against mice and rats
enchant humans with their natural mystery
can be extremely loyal and devoted to their human masters

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 16. The word "dazed" (line 12) as used in the passage means unable to \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Dazed by cold" means confused and unable to think clearly, which is why the traveller mistook the dog for a bear. He was able to see the animal, so D is not right. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage A above) 17. When the author says "... because of his tracking, ..." (line 21) he suggests the type of \_\_\_\_\_\_.

*Options as printed:* A) speed the dog takes to serve   B) job the dog does   C) path or road the dog takes   D) help the dog renders
questions.corrige_markdown:
Piglet found the girl's door by following her scent, which is "tracking". The author is naming the kind of work or service the dog performs, so "job the dog does" (B) and "help the dog renders" (D) both fit; the dog's tracking is a job (tracker dog) and it was also a help to the couple. Speed (A) and path (C) do not describe what tracking is. Because B and D are both defensible, this question is left open for self-assessment.

**Answer: B or D (tracking is the job the dog does, and the help it renders).**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 18. The expression "Piglet smiled and rejoiced on the day of their marriage" (lines 24-25) is an aspect of \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: A dog cannot smile or rejoice at a wedding: human actions are given to an animal. This is personification. There is no contrast between what is said and what is meant (irony), no reference to a famous person or event (allusion) and no "like" or "as" comparison (simile). **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - figures of speech

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Passage B** (questions 19 to 25; the numbers in square brackets are the line numbers printed in the paper)

Everyone in Sammy Agabashian's family was musical, except Sammy. Mama played the piano, Armen played the clarinet, Lucy played the cello, Papa played the violin, Sammy played baseball. Sometimes the family gave a concert together. Usually Papa and Armen played a duet especially written for violin and clarinet. Mama and Lucy always looked beautiful up on the stage in their long silk dresses. Sammy sat in the audience and listened with the others. When Armen or Lucy played alone, Sammy sat in front. He clapped proudly along with Papa. [5] Sometimes the people around them shouted "Bravo!" Mama smiled happily. Everyone said, "Such a talented family. All so musical". Of course, they meant everyone but Sammy.

One day, a man from the newspaper came to take a picture of these musical Agabashians. He grouped all around the piano. Mama sat at the piano bench with her musical instrument spread in front of her. Armen stood next to her with his clarinet, ready to play. So while the picture was taken, Sammy sat and watched, determined [10] to be in the next family picture. He tried to play the violin. "We'll ask Papa to give you lessons", his mother said. Papa tried, Sammy tried; it sounded awful. When Sammy was playing, the cat scratched on the door to be let out.

One day, Sammy walked along the streets and saw a sign. It said there was a painting class for school children [15] on Saturday mornings. Thus every Saturday, Sammy went to the art class.

He learnt how to paint, draw and do programme cover for concerts. He could paint instruments, he could paint dresses blue, green and even black. Sammy worked hard. He worked for days and sometimes he painted in class. Sometimes he worked at home. While he worked, he would hum. One day Armen called, "Look! Look at Sammy's poster!" Lucy said, "Why, this is better than any we've ever had". So this time when the picture [20] was taken, Sammy was right in the middle of the family. Sammy was holding his poster. The picture of all the Agabashians appeared in the newspaper. They were called an artistic family. "Boy!" said Sammy. "Look at that! I finally got in the picture." "Why not?" said his father. "Must everyone play music? You are an artist, and a good one!"

**Questions 19 to 25**

19. The musical instruments used by the Agabashian's family consisted of \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Mama played the piano, Armen the clarinet, Lucy the cello and Papa the violin. Baseball is a sport, not an instrument, and no guitar is mentioned. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 20. Sammy's inability to play well made him feel \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Everyone was musical except Sammy; he sat in the audience while the others played, and he was "determined to be in the next family picture". The feeling this creates is being left out. Nobody rejected him, so "unloved" and "despised" are too strong, and "disappointed" is not what the story stresses. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 21. The first musical instrument that Sammy tried to play was the \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "He tried to play the violin. 'We'll ask Papa to give you lessons'". No other instrument is tried. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 22. When Sammy tried to play the musical instrument, \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "When Sammy was playing, the cat scratched on the door to be let out." The dog, the friends and Jason are not in the story. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the cat scratched on the door to be let out
the dog hid under the bed and howled
Jason quietly rolled his eyes and went home

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 23. At the end of the passage, Sammy was most delighted because he could \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: At the end Sammy cries "Look at that! I finally got in the picture": his delight comes from being part of the family picture. Painting, drawing and doing programme covers are the skills that made it possible. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: be part of the family picture

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage B above) 24. The Agabashians are aptly described as an artistic family because they are \_\_\_\_\_\_.

*Options as printed:* A) painters, musicians and singers   B) painters, baseball players and writers   C) painters, musicians and writers   D) writers, musicians and singers
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the story the family members are musicians (piano, clarinet, cello, violin) and Sammy is a painter who also designs programme covers. Nobody sings, and nobody is a writer, so the printed options A and C each contain one wrong word ("singers" or "writers"), B contains "baseball players", and D has no painter. No option is fully correct, so this question is left open for self-assessment.

**Answer: painters and musicians; the nearest printed option is C (painters, musicians and writers), but "writers" is not supported by the story.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 25. The expression which best describes the message of the passage is "\_\_\_\_\_\_".
questions.corrige_markdown: Sammy was determined to get into the family picture, found a painting class and worked hard until he succeeded. The message is that determination and hard work lead to success. "Make hay while the sun shines" is about using an opportunity in time, "a stitch in time" is about acting early, and "necessity is the mother of invention" is about inventing out of need. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: make hay while the sun shines
determination and hard work lead to success
a stitch in time saves nine
necessity is the mother of invention

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section C - Grammar (7½ marks).** Read the instructions for each question or set of questions carefully before answering. For numbers 26 - 36, choose the best answer that completes each sentence.

26. It is bad to take \_\_\_\_\_\_ property without permission.
questions.corrige_markdown: In a phrase such as "someone else", the possessive 's is added to the last word: "someone else's property". The other forms put the apostrophe in the wrong place or repeat it. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 27. The student always looks up difficult words \_\_\_\_\_\_ his dictionary.
questions.corrige_markdown: One looks up a word "in" a dictionary, because the dictionary contains the word. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 28. Ayuk is the \_\_\_\_\_\_ of the three students.
questions.corrige_markdown: "The ... of the three" compares more than two people, so the superlative is needed. "Brilliant" is a long adjective, so it takes "most", not "-est". "More brilliant" compares only two. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - degrees of comparison

questions.enonce_markdown:
29. Most \_\_\_\_\_\_ are difficult to deal with.

*Options as printed:* A) sister-in-laws   B) sisters - in-law   C) sisters-inlaw   D) sisters-in-laws
questions.corrige_markdown:
The plural of a compound noun such as "sister-in-law" is formed on the main noun: "sisters-in-law". None of the four printed options has this form: A and D put the "s" on "law", B has spaces around the hyphen and a singular "in-law", and C is misspelled. Since no option is correct, this question is left open for self-assessment.

**Answer: sisters-in-law (not printed). Option D, sisters-in-laws, is the closest in shape but is not standard.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 30. Nowadays, many young people are not exposed to reading novels, \_\_\_\_\_\_?
questions.corrige_markdown: The main clause is negative ("are not exposed"), so the tag is positive and uses the same auxiliary "are": "are they?". **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 31. It is high time I \_\_\_\_\_\_ my drugs.
questions.corrige_markdown: After "It is high time" (also "it is time") with a subject, the verb is in the simple past: "It is high time I took my drugs." The past form has a present meaning here. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 32. Laura sells nice \_\_\_\_\_\_ shoes.
questions.corrige_markdown: Shoes made for women are "ladies' shoes": the plural noun "ladies" takes the apostrophe after the s. "Lady's" is singular (shoes of one lady), "ladies" has no apostrophe, and "lady" cannot modify "shoes" in this sense. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 33. My father told me he \_\_\_\_\_\_ no money left in his bank account.
questions.corrige_markdown: In reported speech after "told" (past), the verb is in the past: "he had no money". The verb "have" meaning "possess" is not used in the continuous form, so "was having" and "is having" are wrong, and "has had" does not fit the past reporting verb. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 34. The director's office contains \_\_\_\_\_\_ which \_\_\_\_\_\_ made of expensive wood.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Furniture" is uncountable: it has no plural "furnitures" and takes a singular verb. "Furniture which is made of expensive wood" is therefore correct. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - countable and uncountable nouns

questions.enonce_markdown: 35. They left the hall \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The words describe the verb "left", so two adverbs of the same form are needed: "quickly and quietly". The other options mix an adjective or comparative with an adverb. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 36. The victim \_\_\_\_\_\_ before we went to the scene.
questions.corrige_markdown: Two past events are given, and the dying happened first, so the past perfect "had died" is used with "went". **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
37. (For numbers 37 and 38, choose the sentence that is correctly punctuated.)

A) Amina studies History, French and Mathematics on Saturday.
B) Amina studies history, French and mathematics on Saturday.
C) Amina studies History, French, and mathematics on Saturday.
D) Amina studies history, french and mathematics on Saturday.

*Options as printed:* A) Amina studies History, French and Mathematics on Saturday.   B) Amina studies history, French and mathematics on Saturday.   C) Amina studies History, French, and mathematics on Saturday.   D) Amina studies history, french and mathematics on Saturday.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A list needs commas between the items, with "and" before the last one. "French" is a language and must have a capital letter, so D is wrong, and C capitalises "History" but not "mathematics", which is inconsistent. A and B are both acceptable: standard usage writes school subjects other than languages in small letters (B), while many African school syllabuses write all subject names with capitals (A). The Board's key could be either, so this question is left open for self-assessment.

**Answer: B in standard English; A if all subject names are capitalised as in school timetables.**
themes: O Level English - spelling and punctuation

questions.enonce_markdown:
38. (Choose the sentence that is correctly punctuated.)

A) Walking home, after work, I tried to meditate on my future.
B) Walking home after work I tried, to meditate on my future.
C) Walking home after work I tried to meditate, on my future.
D) Walking home after work, I tried to meditate on my future.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Walking home after work" is an introductory phrase and is followed by one comma before the main clause. Option A adds a needless comma after "home", while B and C place a comma inside the verb phrase, which separates "tried" from "to meditate" and "meditate" from "on my future". **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - spelling and punctuation

choix.texte: Walking home, after work, I tried to meditate on my future.
Walking home after work I tried, to meditate on my future.
Walking home after work I tried to meditate, on my future.
Walking home after work, I tried to meditate on my future.

questions.enonce_markdown: 39. (For numbers 39 and 40, choose the reported form of the given sentences.) "I have lived with my parents for the past ten years", Barry said. Barry said that \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: After the past reporting verb "said", the present perfect "have lived" becomes the past perfect "had lived", and "my" becomes "his". A keeps the present perfect, B uses the simple past, and D changes the form to the continuous. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: he has lived with his parents for the past ten years.
he lived with his parents for the past ten years.
he had lived with his parents for the past ten years.
he had been living with his parents for the past ten years

questions.enonce_markdown: 40. Wase said, "I am well now and can sing." Wase said that \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: In reported speech the pronoun changes from "I" to "she" (or "he"), the verbs go back in time ("am" to "was", "can" to "could") and "now" becomes "then". Only B makes all these changes together. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: I am well now and I could sing
she was well then and could sing
she was well now and could sing
I am well then and can sing

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section D - Vocabulary (5 marks).** Read the instructions for each question or set of questions carefully before answering.

(For numbers 41 and 42, choose the answer that best explains the meaning of the underlined words.)

41. The gift from her grand children surprised her and she went **mute**.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Mute" means unable to speak, and "went mute" means she became speechless with surprise. Confused, shocked and excited describe feelings but not the loss of speech. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 42. The proprietor's son is very **recalcitrant**.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Recalcitrant" means refusing to obey or to change one's behaviour, which is stubborn. It does not mean wicked, lazy or extravagant (spending too much). **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms

questions.enonce_markdown:
43. (Choose the alternative that best gives the opposite of the underlined word.)

Agnes is very **gentle** and people like her for who she is.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Gentle" means calm and kind, and its opposite is "violent". "Jovial" means cheerful, "pumpous" is a misprint of "pompous" (self-important), and "scattered" is unrelated. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms

questions.enonce_markdown:
44. (For numbers 44 - 50, choose the alternative that best completes each sentence.)

44. Everything was done for the \_\_\_\_\_\_ of our guests.
questions.corrige_markdown: The noun is spelled c-o-n-v-e-n-i-e-n-c-e: "convene" and "convenient" keep the letter e after "conv". B, C and D are misspellings. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level English - spelling and punctuation

questions.enonce_markdown: 45. Micro\_\_\_\_\_\_ are used mostly in hospitals.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Micro" + "scopes" gives "microscopes", the instruments used in hospital laboratories to look at tiny things such as blood cells and germs. Microphones are used everywhere, not mostly in hospitals, and "microgram" and "microvision" do not fit the sentence. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
46. As Shang \_\_\_\_\_\_ his head on the pillow, he heard people whispering outside.

*Options as printed:* A) lie   B) lay   C) put   D) laid
questions.corrige_markdown:
The sentence is in the past and "his head" is the object, so a transitive verb in the past is needed. "Laid" (past of "lay", to put down) is the form the question seems to test, since "lie" is a base form and "lay" is the past of the intransitive "lie" ("he lay down"). However "put his head on the pillow" is also perfectly correct English. Because D and C are both defensible, this question is left open for self-assessment.

**Answer: laid (D) is the usual key; put (C) is also correct.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 47. The \_\_\_\_\_\_ date for the drug is not indicated.
questions.corrige_markdown: The noun "expiry" is used before "date" ("expiry date"), as in "sell-by date". "Expiring" and "expired" are participles, and "expire" is a verb. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 48. It is better to be optimistic about life than to be \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The opposite of "optimistic" (hopeful about the future) is "pessimistic" (expecting the worst). Aggressive, arrogant and "antangonistic" (a misprint of "antagonistic") describe attitudes towards other people, not an outlook on life. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms

questions.enonce_markdown: 49. The expression "One good turn deserves another" means \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The proverb says that when someone does you a kindness, you should do a kindness in return: every good deed should be returned. It does not say that a good act "provokes" another, or compare good with evil. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level English - idioms and proverbs

choix.texte: every good deed should be returned
it is good to be good
one good thing done provokes another

questions.enonce_markdown: 50. They divorced because both of them were \_\_\_\_\_\_ compatible.
questions.corrige_markdown: The negative prefix for "compatible" is "in-": "incompatible" means unable to live together in harmony. "Dis-", "un-" and "im-" are not used with this word ("im-" is used before b, m and p). **Answer: D.**
